builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Quantized Edge Inference of a Self-Supervised SAR-Optical Encoder on Commodity x86 Hardware
summary: Replaces FP32/FP16 encoder inference on the GPU or high-precision CPU execution with post-training INT8 quantization, turning numerical precision into a pure cost decision since accuracy is unchanged. Costs an INT8 calibration/conversion step and per-node hardware characterization (AVX2, VNNI, or neither), with negligible accuracy risk (delta within seed spread). Can fail when the target operator set or runtime lacks efficient INT8 kernels for the model's layers, when calibration data is unrepresentative of deployment inputs, or when the device-choice conclusion (iGPU vs CPU) is transferred to different hardware without re-measurement.
rationale: INT8 post-training quantization is mature, requires no retraining or cluster resources, runs on the constrained hardware the reader already has, and the paper demonstrates accuracy neutrality with a measurable latency and energy gain that the reader can verify on their own encoder.
technique: Accuracy-neutral INT8 quantization of ViT encoders for CPU inference

claims.statement: Replaces FP32/FP16 encoder inference on the GPU or high-precision CPU execution with post-training INT8 quantization, turning numerical precision into a pure cost decision since accuracy is unchanged. Costs an INT8 calibration/conversion step and per-node hardware characterization (AVX2, VNNI, or neither), with negligible accuracy risk (delta within seed spread). Can fail when the target operator set or runtime lacks efficient INT8 kernels for the model's layers, when calibration data is unrepresentative of deployment inputs, or when the device-choice conclusion (iGPU vs CPU) is transferred to different hardware without re-measurement.
INT8 quantization changes micro-mAP by only +0.0006 (within seed spread) while reducing CPU latency by 1.45x on a CPU without AVX2 and 1.53x on an AVX2+VNNI reference, also lowering CPU energy.
